name: MCP Server Resource Benchmark
description: Measured resident memory, startup time and tool counts for 11 widely used Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers on Windows 11, together with a concurrent five-server stack. Results. 178-422 MB resident per server (median 188 MB); 0.5-1.9 s warm startup; five-server stack totalling 961.6 MB, cross-checked by two independent measurement paths (psutil and PowerShell WorkingSet64) that agreed exactly. Runtime floors for context: 52 MB bare Node, 15 MB bare Python. Measurement note. npx and uvx are launchers: the parent process holds almost nothing while a child holds the real footprint. Measured directly, the npx parent alone reports 10.3 MB while its full descendant tree holds 189.3 MB, an 18-fold undercount. All RSS figures here are descendant-tree sums sampled 0.4 s after tools/list returned, over 5 iterations per server (3 for two late additions, marked in the data). Canonical page, full method and change log: https://techfuelhq.com/data/mcp-server-bench/
